passages.text: The following should be read in conjunction with "Cautionary Statement Regarding Forward Looking Statements" and our combined consolidated financial statements and notes thereto included in Item 15 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Operating Results Factors Affecting Operating Results Bunge Global SA, a Swiss company, together with its subsidiaries, is a premier agribusiness solutions company, connecting farmers to consumers and delivering essential food, feed and fuel to the world. The commodity nature of the Company's principal products, as well as regional and global supply and demand variations that occur as an inherent part of the business, make volumes an important operating measure. Accordingly, information is included in " Segment Overview and Results of Operations " that summarizes certain items in our consolidated statements of income and volumes by reportable segment. The common unit of measure for all reported volumes is metric tons. 33 Table of Contents Effective in the third quarter of 2025, we changed our reportable segments to align with our new value chain operational structure as a result of the completion of the Acquisition of Viterra. See Note 26- Segment Information to our consolidated financial statements. We also enhanced our volume reporting to align with our new segment reporting structure and with the Company's primary income-generating activities. Volumes are now reported as follows: • Soybean Processing and Refining volumes represent (1) oilseed volumes processed (crushed) during a period, which approximate sales volumes to third parties during the same reporting period (2) merchandised volumes, which represent sales volumes of soybeans to third-party customers during a reporting period and (3) a supplemental refined oil production volume, which will also be provided representing the total refined volume during a reporting period. • Softseed Processing and Refining volumes represent (1) oilseed volumes processed (crushed) during a period, which approximate sales volumes to third parties during the same reporting period (2) merchandised volumes, which represent sales volumes of softseeds to third-party customers during a reporting period and (3) a supplemental refined oil production volume, which will also be provided representing the total refined volume during a reporting period. • Other Oilseeds Processing and Refining volumes represent sales volumes to third-party customers. • Grain Merchandising and Milling volumes represent sales volumes to third-party customers. Further, effective January 1, 2025, Bunge is no longer separately presenting a Sugar and Bioenergy segment, as discussed in Note 26- Segment Information to our consolidated financial statements , nor presenting Core and Non-core segment results. Corresponding prior period amounts have been recast to conform to the current period presentations described above. See also " —The ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine may adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations." These risks could adversely affect our operations, business strategies, and operating results. As a result of our international operations, we are also exposed to currency exchange rate fluctuations. Changes in exchange rates between the U.S. dollar and other foreign currencies, particularly the Brazilian real , Canadian dollar , the euro , and Chinese yuan/renminbi affect our revenues and expenses that are denominated in local currencies, affect farm economics in those regions and may also have a negative impact on the value of our assets located outside of the United States. Additionally, there continues to be a great deal of uncertainty regarding U.S. and global trade policies for companies with multinational operations like ours. In recent years, there has been an increase in populism and nationalism in various countries around the world and consequently historical free trade principles are being challenged. As we continue to operate our business globally, our success will depend, in part, on the nature and extent of any such changes and how well we are able to anticipate, respond to and effectively manage any such changes. Government policies and regulations affecting the agricultural sector and related industries could adversely affect our operations and profitability. Agricultural commodity production and trade flows are significantly affected by government policies and regulations. Governmental policies affecting the agricultural industry, such as taxes (including "windfall profits" taxes), tariffs, duties, subsidies, import and export restrictions, price controls on agricultural commodities, and energy policies (including biofuels mandates), can influence industry profitability, the planting of certain crops versus other uses of agricultural resources, the location and size of crop production, whether unprocessed or processed commodity products are traded, and the volume and types of imports and exports. Additionally, regulation of financial markets and instruments in the United States and internationally may create uncertainty as these laws are adopted and implemented and may impose significant additional risks and costs that could impact our risk management practices. Short-term Debt Bunge's short-term borrowings are typically sourced from various banking institutions and the U.S. commercial paper market. Bunge also borrows from time to time in local currencies in various foreign jurisdictions. Interest expense includes facility commitment fees, amortization of deferred financing costs, the impact of designated interest rate hedges, and charges on certain lending transactions. The weighted-average interest rate on short-term borrowings at December 31, 2025 and 2024 was 5.15 % and 6.22 %, respectively. Revolving Credit Facilities On October 3, 2025, Bunge entered into an unsecured $ 4.2 billion 5-year revolving credit agreement (the "$ 4.2 Billion Revolving Credit Agreement") with a group of lenders, maturing on October 3, 2030. Bunge may from time-to-time request one or more of the existing or new lenders to increase the total participations by an aggregate amount up to $ 1.5 billion, pursuant to an accordion provision. Borrowings will bear interest at Bunge's option, at SOFR plus a margin or the Euribor Rate plus a margin. The $ 4.2 Billion Revolving Credit Agreement replaced an existing $ 3.2 billion 5-year revolving credit agreement which was terminated on October 3, 2025. Bunge had no borrowings outstanding at December 31, 2025, and 2024, under the $ 4.2 Billion Revolving Credit Agreement and the predecessor agreement, respectively. credit_strengths.text: Bunge's global agribusiness and food platform generates substantial revenue, and operating income remains positive despite commodity cyclicality. The current ratio exceeds one, indicating adequate short-term liquidity, while the Altman Z double prime score places the issuer in the safe zone, suggesting a low probability of financial distress under the model's assumptions.

Operating cash flow remains positive, providing a base for debt service even as capital expenditures exceed that cash flow. The company maintains committed revolving credit facilities with no borrowings outstanding under the largest agreement, offering substantial undrawn liquidity that can be accessed to manage working capital swings and refinancing needs.

key_risks.text: The risk factors highlight exposure to currency fluctuations, particularly the Brazilian real, Canadian dollar, euro, and Chinese yuan, which affect revenues, expenses, and asset values. Additionally, uncertainty in U.S. and global trade policies, including tariffs and export restrictions, could disrupt commodity flows and pressure margins for this globally integrated agribusiness.

Debt has increased sharply, with a significant portion maturing within the next twelve months and a large tranche due in year three. The debt note discloses a new revolving credit agreement maturing in year five, but the near-term maturity profile requires refinancing or repayment, which could strain liquidity if cash flow generation remains weak.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is weak relative to sector medians, with operating income covering interest expense at a low multiple. Free cash flow is negative, and the ratio of free cash flow to debt is negative, indicating that internally generated funds are insufficient to service debt after capital expenditures, heightening reliance on external financing or asset sales.

Net leverage, as defined by the analyst context, stands well above the sector median, and the indicative financial risk profile labels the issuer as highly leveraged. The cash flow tier is also weak, with operating cash flow to debt far below the sector median, suggesting limited capacity to deleverage organically without a significant improvement in EBITDA or reduction in debt.

overall_credit_view.text: Bunge's credit profile is pressured by high leverage and weak cash flow coverage, with net leverage exceeding the sector median and an indicative financial risk profile of highly leveraged. The company's substantial debt load, negative free cash flow, and significant near-term maturities raise refinancing risk, although undrawn revolver capacity provides some flexibility.

The company's global scale and essential role in agricultural supply chains support its business risk profile, but commodity price volatility, foreign exchange exposure, and trade policy uncertainty could further weaken cash flows. Shareholder distributions and acquisitions have absorbed cash, contributing to negative free cash flow. A material improvement in operating cash flow or debt reduction is needed to stabilize the credit view.

credit_strengths.text: Bunge的全球農業及食品平台產生可觀收入，而營運收入儘管面對商品週期性仍保持正數。流動比率超過一，顯示短期流動性充足，而Altman Z double prime分數將發行人置於安全區，暗示在該模型假設下財務困境概率偏低。
營運現金流保持正數，為償債提供基礎，即使資本開支超過該現金流。公司維持已承諾的循環信貸融資，而最大協議下並無未償還借款，提供可觀的未提取流動性，可用於管理營運資金波動及再融資需求。

key_risks.text: 風險因素凸顯貨幣波動的敞口，尤其是巴西雷亞爾、加拿大元、歐元及人民幣，影響收入、開支及資產價值。此外，美國及全球貿易政策的不確定性，包括關稅及出口限制，可能擾亂商品流動並對這家全球一體化農業企業的利潤率構成壓力。
債務已急劇增加，其中相當部分將於未來十二個月內到期，而一大筆將於第三年到期。債務票據披露一項將於第五年到期的新循環信貸協議，但近期到期結構需要再融資或償還，若現金流產生仍然疲弱，可能對流動性構成壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率相對於行業中位數偏弱，營運收入以低倍數覆蓋利息開支。自由現金流為負數，而自由現金流對債務比率為負數，顯示內部產生資金在資本開支後不足以償還債務，加大對外部融資或資產出售的依賴。
按分析師背景所定義，淨槓桿遠高於行業中位數，而指示性財務風險狀況將發行人標示為高度槓桿。現金流層級亦偏弱，營運現金流對債務遠低於行業中位數，顯示在EBITDA無顯著改善或債務無減少的情況下，有機去槓桿能力有限。

overall_credit_view.text: Bunge的信貸狀況受高槓桿及疲弱現金流覆蓋所壓力，淨槓桿超過行業中位數，而指示性財務風險狀況為高度槓桿。公司龐大的債務負擔、負自由現金流及顯著的近期到期債務提高再融資風險，儘管未提取的循環信貸額度提供一些靈活性。
公司的全球規模及在農業供應鏈中的關鍵角色支持其業務風險狀況，但商品價格波動、外匯敞口及貿易政策不確定性可能進一步削弱現金流。股東分派及收購已吸收現金，導致負自由現金流。需要營運現金流顯著改善或債務減少以穩定信貸觀點。
